About The Project Office UNOPS Mozambique is a trusted partner in advancing the country’s development priorities and supporting progress toward the Sustainable Development Goals. Working closely with the Government and development partners, UNOPS delivers a range of services—including project management, procurement, and capacity building—to support peacebuilding, expand access to essential services, and strengthen livelihoods. The office plays a vital role in implementing projects that foster resilience and sustainable development, particularly in communities affected by conflict and climate-related challenges. Role Purpose The Project Manager (Infrastructure) is responsible for the effective delivery and day-to-day management of infrastructure projects, which may involve the construction of physical assets, technical outputs, or both. These projects span a range of sectors, including (but not limited to) education, health, transportation, irrigation, and port infrastructure. The Project Manager serves as the focal point for coordination with donors, partners and beneficiaries, ensuring alignment with contractual commitments and UNOPS performance standards. Acting on behalf of the Project Board, the Project Manager ensures that project outputs are delivered within agreed tolerances of time, cost, scope, quality, risk, and benefits. Functions / Key Results Expected Project Delivery and Performance Develop, complete and update the project implementation plan. Implement the approved plan (including establishment of milestones) within tolerances set by the Project Board, including the development of infrastructure designs and coordinating design reviews. Embed sustainability dimensions, including social and gender considerations, and environmental and economic aspects, into the project life span. Manage the production of required outputs, taking responsibility for overall progress and use of resources while initiating corrective action where necessary. Ensure that quality of work packages and deliverables comply with the quality requirements defined in the implementation plan. Liaise with external suppliers or account managers to ensure quality and timely delivery of outputs.Manage acceptance and delivery of work packages. Monitor project progress, control project variances (if any), and manage changes. Identify, anticipate and advise senior management and the project board on mitigating measures against project risks to ensure that benefits to partners and other stakeholders are maximized. Identify and report potential opportunities for UNOPS to the supervisor. Procedures Comply with the organization’s policies and standards, and ensure project information is kept updated in project management systems. Be aware of applicable local laws and regulations, and ensure adherence. This includes international regulations and standards, where applicable, as well as technical standards. Prepare and adapt all relevant plans for approval by the project board, and manage baselines Manage the reporting obligations defined in the implementation plan and legal agreements. Maintain project documentation in an orderly manner for accessibility and audit support when needed. Understand and apply the UNOPS financial rules and regulations. Be accountable for the use of delegation of authority (where applicable) and ensure compliance with relevant policies and standards of ethics. Provide a formal handover of the project to the closure manager when applicable. Support project audit activities, including planning, preparation and coordination during audits and follow-up on audit observations/ recommendations. Prepare and issue regular project and financial reports in accordance with partner and UNOPS requirements for reporting. Regularly review project status and evaluate performance criteria (scope, cost, schedule, and quality) Maintain diaries and progress reports as required by UNOPS standard operating procedures. Provide routine oversight and analysis of delivery data within the dashboard system. Ensure all project team members track and regularly update milestones and targets for the duration of the project life span. Stakeholder Engagement Develop stakeholder engagement strategies and plans. Actively engage stakeholders, take feedback, and adjust as necessary. Establish solid working relationships with the project board (executive, senior users and senior suppliers); clients; and key stakeholders. Enable formulation of project communication plans and monitor effectiveness of project communications. Coordinate stakeholder engagement and communication, ensuring effective timing and interdependency management of communications. Ensure stakeholders are aware of project activities, progress, and exceptions, and are in a position to accept handover outputs. Quality Assurance Work with internal stakeholders to ensure projects comply with audit requirements. Work with procurement/ purchasing personnel to ensure effective interface with suppliers’ quality systems. Coordinate quality reviews of project documents and deliverables. Provide quality control for management outputs (e.g. project documents, reports, etc)) Knowledge Management and Innovation Create a learning environment for the project team, encourage knowledge sharing and training to contribute to longer-term capacity building. Actively interact with other project managers and the wider project management (PM) community, share case studies, lessons learned and best practices. Stay abreast with latest updates and good practices of the profession, participate in training and learning activities for self to advance proficiency and competency. Ensure lessons learned are shared in a timely and appropriate manner. Provide feedback to corporate practice groups on policy and systems, when needed. Provide feedback to functional groups on policies and related guidance to support the continuous improvement of UNOPS policy framework. Personnel Management Organise and structure the project team, ensure clearly defined roles and responsibilities. Provide regular guidance and direction, as needed, and support the team in effectively performing their tasks. Lead and motivate the project management team, and manage performance. Ensure performance reviews are conducted fairly, accurately, and on time. Select, recruit, and train project teams as required, taking gender parity and diversity objectives into account. Ensure safety and security for all project personnel in compliance with the UN Department of Safety and Security (UNDSS) standards. Education Requirements Required Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) in civil, water, electrical, mechanical, structural or other applicable engineering disciplines with 7 years of relevant experience OR Master’s degree (or equivalent) in any of the above with 5 years of relevant experience is required. Desired Project management certification (e.g. PRINCE2, PMI, PEng, CEng, etc) is desired. Required Experience Requirements Relevant experience is work in implementing and managing infrastructure projects (e.g. roads, dams, bridges, irrigation, health, windmills, solar power, ports, etc.), all or some in developing countries, post-conflict environments, or emergency contexts. Experience in defining technical and design requirements is required.. Knowledge of infrastructure quality assurance methodologies and tools is required. Experience in managing infrastructure project risks in a multi-stakeholder context is required. Desired Experience of working in multicultural environments or UN system organizations in a developing country is desired. Experience in development or humanitarian contexts is desired. Experience in contract management is desired. Experience in supporting the development of procurement strategies is desired. Knowledge of FIDIC contracts is desired. Experience of planning and applying health and safety procedures is desired

The Project Manager/Package Manager will lead an integrated multidisciplinary team and manage scope, programme, cost, risk, opportunity, change, quality, interfaces, resources and supply-chain performance. The role will coordinate engineering, commercial, procurement, planning, construction and assurance functions and maintain effective relationships with HS2, the Rail Systems Alliance, suppliers and other project stakeholders. The role will make timely decisions within delegated authority and escalate matters in accordance with SMCJV governance where their value, programme impact, safety, quality, interface, contractual consequence or strategic significance requires higher-level approval. Responsibilities Responsibilities Package leadership and accountability Own the end-to-end management and delivery of allocated work packages, establishing clear scope, objectives, deliverables, responsibilities, resources and delivery strategy. Lead the integrated multidisciplinary package team, setting clear priorities and driving ownership, timely decisions and delivery against agreed commitments. Ensure package scope and requirements remain clearly defined, controlled and traceable throughout the project lifecycle. Programme and delivery management Develop, maintain and manage integrated package delivery plans and programmes aligned with the HRS03 baseline programme and key contractual milestones. Actively manage critical path, dependencies, constraints, interfaces, resources and key deliverables across design, procurement, manufacture, construction, installation, testing and commissioning. Monitor progress and productivity, identify emerging delay or underperformance and implement appropriate mitigation and recovery actions. Commercial and financial performance Own package budget, forecast and cost performance in conjunction with the Commercial team, ensuring expenditure and commitments remain within approved parameters. Manage supply-chain commercial performance, including delivery against subcontract and purchase-order obligations, valuations, variations and emerging liabilities. Ensure change, compensation events, commercial risks and opportunities are identified early, properly evidenced and managed through the appropriate contractual and governance processes. Drive value, productivity and cost efficiency while protecting the JV contractual and commercial position. Risk, opportunity and change management Own and maintain package risks and opportunities, with clear owners, mitigation actions, contingencies and escalation routes. Ensure technical, programme, commercial, safety, quality and interface consequences are understood before changes or commitments are made. Apply effective change control so that scope, programme, cost and contractual impacts are identified, assessed, approved and recorded. Engineering, interfaces and assurance Coordinate design, engineering, procurement, manufacture, installation, testing and commissioning activities to deliver a fully integrated package. Identify and actively manage technical, physical, programme and organisational interfaces with other HRS03 packages and the wider Rail Systems programme. Ensure technical approvals, assurance requirements, inspection and test plans, records, documentation and handover evidence are progressively developed and completed. Ensure defects, non-conformances and technical issues are resolved in a timely and controlled manner. Health, safety, environment and quality Demonstrate visible leadership of health, safety, environment, wellbeing and quality across the package. Ensure activities are properly planned, risk assessed and delivered in accordance with applicable legislation, project requirements, company policies and approved methods of working. Promote a positive safety and quality culture and ensure corrective actions are implemented and closed effectively. Stakeholder and supply-chain leadership Lead and coordinate subcontractors, suppliers, designers, engineers, planners, commercial teams, site teams and assurance functions against agreed package outcomes. Manage supplier and subcontractor performance against contractual obligations, deliverables, programme, quality and productivity expectations. Maintain effective package-level relationships with HS2, the Rail Systems Alliance and other internal and external stakeholders within delegated authority. Chair package progress and coordination meetings, ensuring decisions, actions and accountabilities are clearly recorded and driven to closure. Governance, reporting and performance Provide accurate and timely reporting on programme, cost, forecast, risk, opportunity, change, safety, quality, supply-chain performance and delivery status. Maintain appropriate package registers, action logs, risk and opportunity records, programme updates and other project controls. Operate in accordance with SMCJV governance, delegated authority, change control and reporting requirements. Make decisions at the appropriate level and promptly escalate issues where their significance exceeds delegated authority or threatens wider project outcomes. Drive the successful completion, testing, commissioning, documentation, acceptance and handover of the allocated package scope. Key Performance Indicators Delivery against agreed programme, milestones and package commitments. Package cost performance, forecast accuracy and management of financial commitments. Health, safety, environment, wellbeing and quality performance. Effective management and closure of risks, opportunities, change, interfaces, defects and non-conformances. Subcontractor and supplier performance, productivity and delivery reliability. Accuracy and timeliness of project controls, reporting and escalation. Successful testing, commissioning, assurance, acceptance and handover of package scope. Essential Knowledge, Skills, and Experience Demonstrable experience managing construction, rail, infrastructure or multidisciplinary engineering projects or work packages through multiple lifecycle stages. Proven ability to lead multidisciplinary project/package teams and coordinate engineering, commercial, procurement, planning, construction and assurance functions. Strong understanding of project management, project controls, programme management, risk and opportunity management, change control and project governance. Commercial awareness with experience managing budgets, forecasts, contracts, subcontractors, suppliers and supply-chain performance. Experience managing complex interfaces, dependencies and stakeholders in a multi-party project environment. Good understanding of health, safety, environmental and quality requirements applicable to major infrastructure delivery. Ability to interpret technical drawings, specifications, programmes, commercial information and project documentation and translate these into delivery actions. Strong leadership, planning, communication, problem-solving, negotiation and stakeholder-management skills. Desirable Experience of major UK rail or regulated infrastructure programmes, preferably involving rail systems, power or complex systems integration. Working knowledge of NEC3 and/or NEC4 contracts and associated change and early-warning processes. Experience of testing, commissioning, technical assurance, acceptance and handover. Experience working within a joint venture, alliance or similarly complex collaborative delivery environment. Qualifications Essential HNC/HND, degree or equivalent demonstrable experience in construction, engineering, project management or a relevant discipline. Desirable APM, PRINCE2 or equivalent recognised project-management qualification. Relevant professional membership or progress toward professional membership, for example APM, CIOB, ICE or an appropriate engineering institution. About Us Costain helps to improve people’s lives with integrated, leading edge, smart infrastructure solutions across the UK’s energy, water, transportation and defence markets. We help our clients improve their business performance by increasing capacity, improving customer service, safeguarding security, enhancing resilience, decarbonising and delivering increased efficiency. Our vision is to be the UK’s leading smart infrastructure solutions company. We will achieve this by focusing on blue chip clients whose major spending plans are underpinned by strategic national needs, regulatory commitments, legislation or essential performance requirements. We offer our clients leading edge solutions that are digitally optimised through the following five services which cover the whole lifecycle of their assets: future-shaping strategic consultancy; consultancy and advisory; digital technology solutions; asset optimisation and complex programme delivery.
